title: As a power user, the tool documents which input formats convert to which outputs, so I can check a pair before trying it
As a power user, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files convert to PDF and between office formats
As a power user, common image formats (PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC, SVG) convert with control over quality, size, and compression
As a power user, audio and video transcode between formats with control over codec, bitrate, and resolution
As a developer, markup and e-book formats (Markdown, HTML, LaTeX, EPUB, DOCX) convert between each other
As a power user, archives (ZIP, 7z, RAR) extract and repack as part of a conversion
As a power user, document conversion preserves layout, fonts, images, and tables rather than flattening them
As a developer, file metadata is preserved through a conversion or strippable on request
As a developer, a failed conversion reports why it failed (unsupported feature, corrupt input) instead of silently emitting a broken file
As an ops lead, I can convert a whole folder or list of files in one run, with per-file results
As a developer, a documented command converts a file in one line, usable from scripts and CI
As a developer, the tool returns meaningful exit codes and logs, so a pipeline can tell success from failure without parsing prose
As an ops lead, I can chain steps (convert, then optimize, then deliver) into one job or watched workflow
As a developer, a documented API takes an upload or URL, runs the conversion as a job with visible status, and returns the output file
As a developer, finished jobs notify my system by callback instead of making me poll
As a developer, official client libraries exist for mainstream languages, versioned and maintained by the vendor
As a developer, a free tier, trial, or sandbox lets me test real conversions before paying
As a power user, conversion runs entirely on my machine, and the vendor states that files are never uploaded
As a developer, the conversion engine runs inside my own infrastructure as a library, container, or server I operate
As a power user, a one-off conversion works in the browser with nothing installed
As an ops lead, a hosted converter documents how long uploads are kept and when converted files are deleted
As a developer, file-size, duration, and concurrency limits are documented, so I can size jobs before hitting a wall
As an ops lead, the converter treats untrusted input safely: scripts and macros are read as content, never executed
